title: Pinarello trickles down Dogma X features to new X Series range
content:
Cyclist
Pinarello trickles down Dogma X features to new X Series range  

PInarello claims that its updated X Series endurance bike range strikes the perfect balance between comfort and performance.

According to Fausto Pinarello, the brand’s president, ‘The all-new X Series represents a significant step forward for Pinarello’s endurance collection. We wanted to focus on what real-world cyclists actually need during long rides on everyday road surfaces – unmatched comfort and vibration-absorption without losing any performance.’

As with the top spec Dogma X, which received an update in July and which Pinarello claims is the lightest endurance bike in the world, the new X Series bikes have a simplified design which swaps the multiple cross-braces in the seatstays for a single split, which meets the seat tube in just two places. 

The seatstays are also placed lower down than in the previous generation bikes, which Pinarello claims helps to disperse road vibrations more effectively and minimise rebound for a smoother ride.

While the updated Dogma X stuck at 35mm tyre clearance, the X Series bikes offer space for 40mm tyres. There’s no mention from Pinarello of mudguard mounts, which were a feature that it didn’t include in the Dogma X update. Frame geometry remains unchanged and is engineered to be more comfortable than the Dogma X, with a higher stack and shorter reach.

There’s a new seatpost design that Pinarello says offers 10mm of fore/aft flex to help smooth the ride further. It has added integrated down tube storage to the new X Series bikes, complete with a tool bag.  

Like Pinarello’s F Series bikes, which received an update a year ago, the new X Series is available in multiple carbon fibre layups, using a less exotic mix of carbon fibre than the M40X used for the Dogma bikes. 

The higher spec X9 and X7 are built of T900 carbon, the X5 and X3 use T700, while the X1 is made of T600 carbon fibre. All but the X1 swap to an elliptical steerer, again copying the Dogma X, and allowing fully internal cable routing. Pinarello claims this improves torsional stiffness and steering precision.

The X1 has the same round steerer as the previous generation X Series bikes, offering compatibility with mechanical groupsets for the entry-level bike. The X1 doesn’t include the in-frame storage of the higher spec bikes either.

Pinarello X Series outline specs and prices

Pinarello X9

  • Groupset: Shimano Dura-Ace
  • Wheels: Most Ultrafast 45 DB 
  • Price: £N/A / $11,000 / €11,000

Pinarello X7

  • Groupset: Shimano Ultegra 
  • Wheels: Most Ultrafast 45 DB 
  • Price: £6,500 / $8,200 / €7,900

Pinarello X5

  • Groupset: Shimano 105 Di2 
  • Wheels: Most Fast 45 DB 
  • Price: £5,000 / $5,500 / €5,100

Pinarello X3

  • Groupset: Shimano 105 Di2 
  • Wheels: DT Swiss A1800 DB 
  • Price: £4,000 / $4,750 / €4,500

Pinarello X1

  • Groupset: Shimano 105
  • Wheels: Most Fact 27 DB wheels
  • Price: £3,000 / $2,950 / €3,200
